issues.body: `ends_operand` continues to exclude `>` because that byte can be the greater-than operator, but `>` also terminates an IRI operand. For `FILTER(<http://ex/a><1&&FLTR(?o)&&?b>2)`, scanning the first IRI leaves `prev == '>'`; the following compact `<` is therefore treated as an IRIREF opener. Its body remains IRIREF-legal until the later `>`, so `iriref_end` skips over `FLTR` and no `FILTER` suggestion is produced. This is the same major correctness finding as round 3, and no added test exercises that counterexample.
issues.fix_hint: Track the preceding token's lexical kind rather than only its final byte, so an IRI operand ending in `>` is distinguishable from the greater-than operator. Add a real-path regression using `FILTER(<http://ex/a><1&&FLTR(?o)&&?b>2)` that asserts `FLTR` suggests `FILTER`, while retaining a case where a greater-than operator is followed by a genuine IRI.
issues.title: IRI operand before compact less-than still swallows diagnostics

verdict.summary: Round 4 is stagnant: the round-3 acceptance-set mismatch remains in the submitted implementation. `opens_iriref` still reduces the preceding token to one byte, while `ends_operand` still excludes `>`. Thus a completed IRI operand followed immediately by a less-than operator is misclassified as the start of another IRIREF; a later `>` can cause the scanner to skip the misspelled keyword. The newly added compact-comparison tests cover variables and call results before `<`, but not the exact IRI-operand counterexample from round 3.
